report.summary: Both failures are the same test-side bug: the BooksPage page object clicks a test id that does not exist. The page object at tests/support/pages.py:44 uses get_by_test_id("add-books"), but the template at app/templates/books.html:9 renders data-testid="add-book". Fix the locator in pages.py first; both tests should then get past the click, and the product code does not need to change.

causes.title: BooksPage.add clicks non-existent data-testid "add-books"
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add() in tests/support/pages.py locates the submit button with get_by_test_id("add-books"). The Books template names that button data-testid="add-book" (singular). The locator matches nothing, so Playwright waits the full 5000 ms and raises TimeoutError at the click, before any assertion runs. Both UI tests that call books.add() fail at this same line. The login UI tests are not in the failure list, which fits a problem limited to the books page object. The application is correct here, so this is a test bug.
evidence: Call log: "waiting for get_by_test_id(\"add-books\")" (identical in both failures, tests\ui\test_books_ui.py:13 and :42)
Other locators in pages.py (title, author, year, book-row, delete-book, logout) match the template, so the mismatch is specific to add-books.
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/support/pages.py line 44, change get_by_test_id("add-books") to get_by_test_id("add-book"). Optionally make BooksPage hold the locator as a named attribute so it is defined in one place. Then rerun tests/ui/test_books_ui.py. Once the click works, check the assertions in test_future_year_shows_error_and_keeps_input, since they have not run yet.
